examples.label: Full enumeration with a WPVulnDB API token for CVE mapping

notes: Aggressive plugin detection (--enumerate ap) is loud and slow but finds vulnerable plugins passive mode misses. A WPVulnDB API token is what maps versions to CVEs - without it you only get a plugin list.

recommended.note: Manual fingerprinting that scopes this scan.
Feed enumerated usernames into a password attack.
Pivot to a plugin exploit if a vulnerable one is found.

name: WPScan - Enumerate Themes/Plugins/Users
description: Automated WordPress scanner. --enumerate finds plugins, themes, and users; an API token adds known-vulnerability data from the WPScan database.

defense.why_it_works: WPScan queries WordPress-specific paths (/wp-json/wp/v2/users for users, plugin readme.txt for versions) and the WPScan Vulnerability Database, correlating findings against known CVEs.
defense.prerequisites: HTTP access to the WordPress site. A WPScan API token is needed for CVE lookups but enumeration works without it.
defense.impact: Complete enumeration: WordPress version, all active plugins with CVE matches, themes, and registered usernames - providing the full attack surface in one command.
defense.detection: Rapid sequential requests to /wp-json/wp/v2/users, /readme.txt, plugin readme paths from one IP. User-Agent 'WPScan' in access logs.
defense.artifacts: Web server access logs (WPScan UA, /wp-json/ requests) | WAF/IDS alerts for WPScan signatures
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web sourcetype=access_combined (uri_path=\"/wp-json/wp/v2/users\" OR uri_path=\"/?author=\" OR uri_path=\"/wp-content/plugins/\")
| stats count dc(uri_path) as urls by clientip, useragent, bin(_time, 1m)
| where urls>20 OR count>100
defense.elastic_kql: event.category:web AND source.ip:* AND url.path:("/wp-json/wp/v2/users" OR "/?author=" OR "/wp-content/plugins/")
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| summarize urls=dcount(csUriStem), hits=count() by cIP, csUserAgent, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where urls > 20 or hits > 100
| sort by hits desc
// wpscan application fingerprinting/enumeration (path burst, scanner UA)
defense.prevention: Disable the WP REST API user endpoint. Limit login attempts. Block WPScan User-Agent at WAF. Keep all plugins updated.
defense.misconfiguration: WordPress REST API unauthenticated user endpoint (/wp/v2/users) accessible, leaking all usernames. Plugin directories expose readme.txt with exact version numbers.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# WP default
# GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users -> returns all usernames
# GET /wp-content/plugins/mail-masta/readme.txt -> version 1.0
defense.evasion: Use --random-user-agent flag. Use --throttle to slow below WAF rate thresholds. Route through Tor with --proxy.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review IIS Web Server logs, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Scans a WordPress site for enumerable components with WPScan:
  wpscan --url http://<url>   point at the target
  --enumerate                 enumerate plugins, themes, and users (u,vp,vt to scope)
  --api-token <token>         add known-vulnerability data from the WPScan database
Maps the attack surface and flags vulnerable plugins/themes; it can also brute-force logins (-U/-P --password-attack xmlrpc).
